claim: PAC Prediction Sets for LLMs of Code (ICML 2023) is the first paper to construct PAC prediction sets for generative code models, representing the set as a partial program (AST with uncertain nodes replaced by holes).
stance_target: novelty of distribution-free/PAC prediction-set guarantees for code generation in general
scope_conditions: PICARD (T5 SQL semantic parsing), Codex (Python + ~12 languages), program/AST granularity, 2023
quoted_support: This is the first research contribution that generates PAC prediction sets for generative code models.

claim: PAC prediction sets for code operate at AST/program granularity (which subtree nodes are uncertain), not at unit-test/requirement granularity, and impose a monotonicity constraint on risk plus a single-label assumption that RisCoSet (2026) later identifies as limiting.
stance_target: per-requirement conformal risk control for code remaining open
scope_conditions: program-level structured prediction, single valid label assumption
quoted_support: existing techniques have largely targeted settings where the space of labels is simple, so prediction sets can be arbitrary subsets of labels
